runs.content: Tuesday's rotation focus is AI & Tech + Technology. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-07), log.md shows only routine automated Finance activity (a growth-value-tracker refresh, a portfolio-management-briefing, and a no-trade Labor Day paper-trading entry) with nothing new in AI & Tech or Technology to review — memory/index.md's Domain Content Status for both domains is unchanged since the last deep-dive. Deep-reading the AI & Tech and Technology overview pages plus a handful of previously-unexamined source pages in both domains (Blodget's AI-bubble piece, the Nvidia $500bn backstop/Theseus Infrastructure digest, SemiAnalysis's CXMT writeup, and Technology's GitHub Copilot and Meta-AI-briefing source pages) surfaced one genuinely new, non-duplicate cross-domain connection: GitHub Copilot's June 2026 switch to token-based billing (technology/source-github-copilot-token-billing-2026 — developers seeing $29-to-$750+/month cost jumps, concentrated specifically in 'multi-agent, long-running tasks') is a live, dated, consumer-facing instance of exactly the token-cost-adoption-barrier Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora's piece (ai-tech/source-arora-token-pricing-2026-07-09) treats as a forward-looking constraint five weeks later — Arora's own reference catalyst is specifically 'agentic coding' token efficiency, the same product category Copilot's backlash sits in. Neither page cites the other; the Technology-domain source page only cross-links to its own domain overview. No new investigation idea cleared the bar today (candidates considered — the Theseus Infrastructure JV's consumer-electricity-price-guarantee term, and Fred's own Claude Code cost exposure — were either already covered by existing open threads or too speculative to state as a concrete next step), and nothing in the existing open sections showed clear signs of resolution.

Monday's rotation focus is Finance + Crypto. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-06), log.md shows only two routine automated updates — the growth-value-tracker and sector-performance-tracker weekly refreshes — with no new clippings or portfolio moves to review. Deep-reading both trackers plus Crypto's overview and portfolio pages surfaced one genuinely new, non-duplicate investigation idea: Ray Dalio's March 2026 piece on the Strait of Hormuz ([[finance/investor-letters/source-dalio-strait-of-hormuz]]) argued, five months ahead of the fact, that control of the Strait would be the single decisive flashpoint of the Iran war. On 2026-08-31 that materialized almost exactly as described — US strikes on Iranian sites, a WTI spike — and the paper-trading book opened a live trade (OXY) explicitly citing the resulting sector tailwind. A grep of the paper-trading trade log turned up five more trades (COP, CMCL, ICE, CMCSA, XOM) independently citing the same Strait-of-Hormuz risk premium as a catalyst across the past several months, none of which cross-link Dalio's own analysis — a real, recurring pattern (his macro framework has been quietly playing out in the simulated book for months) rather than a one-off. Today's sector tracker refresh independently confirms Energy is the tracker's best value/momentum sector this run, reinforcing that the pattern is still live. No new cross-domain connection cleared the bar today (Crypto's BTC recovery to $79.7k and the sector tracker's other moves are continuations of already-logged threads), and nothing in the existing open sections showed clear signs of resolution.
